confirmedThemeFixes.title: IBM Plex Sans Arabic font enqueued twice with same handle + 3rd @import
confirmedThemeFixes.fix: Target file 1 — functions.php (child theme): DELETE the duplicate block at lines 1793-1806 in full: the docblock (1794-1796), the function `edublink_child_enqueue_fonts() {...}` (1797-1805), and its `add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', 'edublink_child_enqueue_fonts', 1);` (1806). KEEP `learnsimply_enqueue_ibm_plex_font` (lines 29-41) as the single source of truth. Verify no other call site references `edublink_child_enqueue_fonts` (grep confirms only the definition + its own add_action exist) before deleting. Net effect: removes one redundant hook callback; rendered HTML output is unchanged (handle dedup already collapsed it). Target file 2 — views/sections/home/features-section.twig:5 (the actual render-blocking fix): REMOVE the `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter...&family=Readex+Pro...&display=swap');` line from the inline `<style>`. Replace by enqueuing it properly in functions.php so it is parallel-loaded and version-controlled — e.g. inside the existing `learnsimply_enqueue_ibm_plex_font()` add a second `wp_enqueue_style('ls-home-inter-readex', 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600&family=Readex+Pro:wght@200;300;400;500;600&display=swap', array(), null);` (or conditionally only on the front page via `is_front_page()` to avoid loading it site-wide, since it's only used by the homepage features section). This eliminates the render-blocking `@import` while preserving the Inter/Readex Pro fonts the section depends on. Single PR, both files; run `npm run audit` (Playwright) on the homepage after deploy + cache flush to confirm fonts still render and no layout shift.
confirmedThemeFixes.where: CONFIRMED present in current HEAD (9a7a78b). Two identical font-enqueue functions both still exist and both register unconditionally: (1) functions.php:33 `learnsimply_enqueue_ibm_plex_font()` hooked at functions.php:32 `add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', ..., 1)`; (2) functions.php:1797 `edublink_child_enqueue_fonts()` hooked at functions.php:1806 `add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', ..., 1)`. Both call `wp_enqueue_style('ibm-plex-sans-arabic', 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=IBM+Plex+Sans+Arabic:wght@100;200;300;400;500;600;700&display=swap', array(), null)` — byte-identical handle + URL. No conditional guards on either (the only nearby `if` statements at lines ~21-24 belong to the REST /wp/v2/users disable code, unrelated). NUANCE: because WP `wp_enqueue_style` dedupes by handle, the font is emitted only ONCE in the rendered HTML — so this is duplicate/dead PHP (maintenance hazard + a wasted second hook callback), NOT a double network request. The genuinely render-blocking item is the 3rd font call: views/sections/home/features-section.twig:5 has `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600&family=Readex+Pro:wght@200;300;400;500;600&display=swap')` inside an inline `<style>` block. That twig IS live (included via views/front-page.twig:20, and the @import renders at homepage.html:2972). `@import` inside `<style>` is render-blocking and uncontrolled by WP enqueue. Title's "enqueued twice" is technically dead-code duplication rather than double-output; the render-blocking concern is real and lives in the twig @import. SOLO-theme (PR Omar merges himself).

confirmedThemeFixes.title: instructor.title property doesn't exist on Timber User → always 'مدرب' fallback
confirmedThemeFixes.fix:
SOLO-theme (PR Omar merges himself). Edit views/single-course.twig:285. Replace:

{{ instructors[0].title ?: 'مدرب' }}

with:

{{ instructor_title }}

Rationale for correcting the proposed fix: the original sketch (`instructor_title|default('مدرب')`) is functionally safe but slightly off — `instructor_title` is ALWAYS set (functions.php:1205, value 'مهندس برمجيات'), so the `|default('مدرب')` branch is dead code, and its 'مدرب' default contradicts the value shown by the 16 other templates. Use bare `{{ instructor_title }}` to exactly match every other instructor-role output in the theme (consistency + shows the intended 'مهندس برمجيات'). The context var requires no PHP change — it is already merged via Timber::context() in single-course.php:30. confirmedThemeFixes.where:
CONFIRMED still present. views/single-course.twig:285 reads `

{{ instructors[0].title ?: 'مدرب' }}

` exactly as claimed (checkout at origin/main HEAD 9a7a78b). confirmedThemeFixes.title: Hero stats hardcoded (+1000 students, 98%, +7Y)
confirmedThemeFixes.fix:
Correction to the proposed fix: do NOT compute the "+1000 students" figure from tutor_utils enrolled counts. `count_enrolled_users_by_course()` is per-course, so summing across courses double-counts any student enrolled in multiple courses (Ahmed's catalog is exactly that — multi-course buyers), producing an inflated/wrong number. And `98%` satisfaction + `+7Y` experience have no DB source at all — they are pure marketing claims. So an "auto-computed" hero stat would be misleading, not an improvement. Solid fix = make all three editable via WP theme-mods (Customizer) with the current literals as defaults, so Omar/Ahmed change them in wp-admin without touching code, and the rendered value never goes stale or fake: 1) front-page.php — before `Timber::render(...)` (around line 397), add: ```php // Hero stats (editable via Customizer; current values are defaults) $context['hero_stats'] = array( array( 'value' => get_theme_mod( 'ls_hero_stat1_value', '+1000' ), 'label' => get_theme_mod( 'ls_hero_stat1_label', 'طالب بدأوا من الصفر' ), ), array( 'value' => get_theme_mod( 'ls_hero_stat2_value', '98%' ), 'label' => get_theme_mod( 'ls_hero_stat2_label', 'رضا الطلاب عن المحتوى' ), ), array( 'value' => get_theme_mod( 'ls_hero_stat3_value', '+7Y' ), 'label' => get_theme_mod( 'ls_hero_stat3_label', 'خبرة في تعليم البرمجة' ), ), ); ``` 2) views/sections/home/hero-section.twig — replace the hardcoded `stats-row` block (lines 151-170) with a loop over context (escaped output; no |safe needed since these are admin-set plain strings): ```twig
{% for s in hero_stats %}

{{ s.value }}

{{ s.label }}

{% endfor %}
``` 3) (Optional, recommended) register the 6 settings in the theme Customizer so they're actually editable in wp-admin (functions.php → `customize_register` hook). If you skip step 3, the theme-mods still work but can only be set programmatically; with defaults in place the page renders identically to today either way, so it is a zero-visual-regression change. Note: hero-section.twig is included by front-page.twig, which is rendered ONLY by front-page.php — so adding `hero_stats` to that one context is sufficient; no other template renders this partial.
